public_rationale: OpenAI had computing and prospective distribution relationships that deserve consideration as possible protections beyond its brand. Their existence does not establish a durable moat, and the available evidence does not establish the absence of one either. Calling every partnership a moat would stretch the claim against Marcus; treating competing models as proof that no moat existed would stretch it in his favor.
limitations: The cited announcements predate the target snapshot and are context only.
Public partnership announcements omit contractual and commercial details needed to measure competitive protection.

our_interpretation: A moat means a durable competitive protection, such as substantial switching costs, privileged access to scarce resources, or protected distribution. Merely possessing useful assets does not establish a moat.
The qualification expresses uncertainty about a checkable business assessment; it is not treated as a conditional forecast.
This describes OpenAI's competitive position on the post date. A market position can be observed contemporaneously, so the target is July 24, 2024, rather than a financial reporting quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that customers had effective substitutes and that OpenAI lacked material competitive protection beyond its brand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence identifies at least one material, durable protection against competition that OpenAI possessed independently of brand recognition.
